sourceHeadings: Retained replay references and safe removal
file04Operations.role: Live bytes. File 04 requires the eight generation properties, journals every lifecycle operation, requires recovery at each write/fsync/rename/pointer transition, fail-closed quarantine of ambiguous bytes/state, prepare/commit/abort migration with declared no-return, and names this harness as injecting faults at every journal write/fsync/rename/pointer transition and every migration prepare/commit/abort/no-return boundary. It covers atomic activation/rollback, complete dependency/state/permission closure, conflicting project locks, leases/refcounts, process death, reference-safe removal, and retained-evidence reachability. Clean-machine and revocation-aware repair remain joined through DR-G06, DR-G08, and DR-G11. The concrete lock/journal/lease mechanism is open. Removal deactivates; V2 does not invent a loss code. This specification does not rewrite those bytes.

namedCorpusClasses.exactByteIntent: Once authored: per D-002 platform, digest-pinned crash injections at every named journal write, fsync, rename, and pointer transition, and at every migration prepare, commit, abort, and no-return boundary. Each record retains the injected site, the pre-crash generation identity, the post-recovery observer-visible generation (old or new, never mixed), and whether recovery resumed or restored an exact verified generation or fail-closed/quarantined. This class names crash-injection sites. It does not choose an on-disk journal format, lock-file grammar, lease API, solver, filesystem layout, or reviewed-equivalent of atomic rename. Those mechanisms remain reserved. This specification does not apply lifecycle-generation-contract.v2. Repair-media crash injection remains joined through DR-G06, DR-G08, and DR-G11 and is not this class. Fixtures are unauthored.
namedCorpusClasses.passProperty: After each named crash site, observers see generation N or generation N+1, never a mixture. Ambiguous bytes or state fail closed and quarantine. A skipped named site is not a waiver. Recovery does not invent a journal implementation, a D9/loss code, or a self-update. Pass all four D-002 platforms. Windows is not a cell.

namedCorpusClasses.exactByteIntent: Once authored: per D-002 platform, digest-pinned records of two projects concurrently selecting incompatible component/artifact closures (file 04: different projects may concurrently select conflicting component versions). Each record retains both lock pin-sets (signed index snapshot, component/artifact closure, platform alternative, subprotocol/state formats, and policy constraints as file 04 names them) and proves generations do not mix. This class is cross-project conflicting locks. It does not invent a same-project concurrent-analyze class, a live-lease activation class, or a two-cache-writer class. It does not execute G16 lock-lane results. It does not fork DR-103 lockSchema and does not produce a lock. Window meaning of pinned format identifiers remains DR-111. Fixtures are unauthored.
namedCorpusClasses.passProperty: Two projects may hold incompatible closures at the same time. A process leased to generation A cannot observe generation B's bytes as if they were A's. Mixing fails. Waiver of a mixed generation is not a skipped cell. Pass all four D-002 platforms.

namedCorpusClasses.exactByteIntent: Once authored: per D-002 platform, digest-pinned process-death records during a journaled lifecycle operation. Each record retains the held lease/refcount, the death event, lease reap (explicit or process-death reaped), and fail-closed recovery of the generation pointer. This class is generation/lease crash-safety. It is not G21 component process-tree kill/reap, not G09 grant-linearization process death, and not G12 doctor crash/backup/external-store cases. Fixtures are unauthored.
namedCorpusClasses.passProperty: A dead process's lease is reaped. Ambiguous generation state fails closed. Uncommitted publication is not visible as a mixture. G21, G09, and G12 are not scored here. Pass all four D-002 platforms.

retainedEvidence.measures: Activation, migration commit/abort/no-return, and rollback publication are atomic. Observers see old or new, never a mixture. Activation never mutates verified bytes in place (file 04 immutable-installs bullet consumed here, not as a sixth live-cell member). Prepare has no observer-visible authority change. Abort leaves old generation state intact.
retainedEvidence.exactByteIntent: Once authored: per D-002 platform, digest-pinned records for activation, rollback, and migration prepare/commit/abort/no-return, on the crash-injection class and the conflicting-project-locks class, showing observer-visible generation identity before and after. Prepare does not change authority. Commit publishes old-or-new. Abort leaves old. No-return is declared; this specification does not invent window numbers (DR-111). In-place mutation of verified bytes fails. This member does not score G08 trust-state machines or DR-110 core-byte rollback. Fixtures are unauthored.
retainedEvidence.passProperty: Observers of a project see generation N or N+1, never a mix of dependency, permission, executable, schema, state, or migration halves. In-place mutation fails. A mixed publication fails. Self-update rollback is not scored. Pass all four D-002 platforms. Waiver of mixed publication is forbidden.
retainedEvidence.suppliedBy: crash-injection corpus class and conflicting-project-locks corpus class. Not authored.

retainedEvidence.measures: After a crash, ambiguous bytes or state fail closed and quarantine. Recovery may resume or restore only an exact verified generation permitted by current trust. Every lifecycle operation is journaled and lease-scoped (file 04). Publication requires durable staged files/directories/journal, same-filesystem atomic rename or a reviewed equivalent, and recovery at each write/fsync/rename/pointer transition. This member names those obligations; it does not choose the journal or the reviewed equivalent.
retainedEvidence.exactByteIntent: Once authored: per D-002 platform, digest-pinned recovery records for the crash-injection class and the process-death class, pairing each injected site with either (a) resume/restore of an exact verified generation or (b) fail-closed quarantine of ambiguous bytes/state. No invented D9, loss, or purge code. No self-update. Quarantine is required; on-disk quarantine format is reserved. Whether current trust permits restoring a generation is joined to DR-112/G08 and is not this member designing the ceremony. Fixtures are unauthored.
retainedEvidence.passProperty: Ambiguous state is not published. Fail-closed holds. A skipped crash site fails. An invented D9 or loss code fails this specification. G08, G12, and G21 are not scored as this member. Pass all four D-002 platforms. No waiver for ambiguous authoritative state.
retainedEvidence.suppliedBy: crash-injection corpus class and process-death corpus class. Not authored.

retainedEvidence.measures: Activation atomically publishes the dependency, permission/confinement, executable, schema, state, and migration closure (file 04). Live-cell punctuation keeps dependency/state/permission as one member. This is generation-closure atomicity, not G09 permission truth, not G19 durable state-byte class, and not G16 CI lock-lane results.
retainedEvidence.exactByteIntent: Once authored: per D-002 platform, digest-pinned closure records bound to EV-1's generation identity, covering the published dependency, permission/confinement, executable, schema, state, and migration halves as one old-or-new set. A half from generation N mixed with a half from N+1 fails. Permission/confinement here is the published generation closure, not G09 requested/granted/denied tables and not permission-fx corpora. State here is the generation's schema/state half, not G19 class/owner/writer assignment. This specification does not fork DR-103 lockSchema and does not assign DR-124 state class. Fixtures are unauthored.
retainedEvidence.passProperty: The published closure is complete and old-or-new. A mixed half fails. G09, G16, and G19 are not scored. Pass all four D-002 platforms.
retainedEvidence.suppliedBy: crash-injection corpus class and conflicting-project-locks corpus class. Not authored.

retainedEvidence.measures: Active processes hold generation leases/refcounts and open references needed for safe completion/recovery (file 04). Each operation pins the project-selected generation for its entire lifetime (file 04 third bullet consumed here, not as a sixth live-cell member). A later project lock change starts a new operation, never mutates a live one. Lease release is explicit or process-death reaped. A lease is not a secret and not a trust decision.
retainedEvidence.exactByteIntent: Once authored: per D-002 platform, digest-pinned lease/refcount records for the crash-injection, conflicting-project-locks, and process-death classes, showing the held generation, the operations leased to it, and reap on explicit release or process death. A live leased process cannot be collected. This specification does not choose fcntl, sqlite, or a custom lease API. Fixtures are unauthored.
retainedEvidence.passProperty: A live process holds a lease on its generation. Crash recovery consults leases. A reaped lease is not a live root. Mixing leased generation A with generation B bytes fails. G21 process-tree reaping is not this member. Pass all four D-002 platforms.
retainedEvidence.suppliedBy: crash-injection corpus class, conflicting-project-locks corpus class, and process-death corpus class. Not authored.

retainedEvidence.measures: Remove and GC cannot delete bytes/state referenced by locks, active processes, retained evidence, rollback slots, or prepared migrations (file 04 generation-property bullet). File 04 reachability (lines 123-139) names five roots: project/operation locks and active generation leases; retained authoritative evidence and custody records; active/provisional generations and rollback slots; prepared migrations and repair state; and binding retention policy/tombstones. Removal deactivates; it does not invent a typed purge result. Preview does not ship authoritative sealed closure (D-002). The retained-evidence root is named; for preview it applies only to whatever operational-metadata / doctor records DR-124 assigns. The repair-state root remains joined to DR-110/G08. It does not pull DR-113 into the preview and does not invent a sealed-Run class.
retainedEvidence.exactByteIntent: Once authored: per D-002 platform, digest-pinned removal records showing a generation remains while any named root holds it (project/operation locks, active generation leases, preview-honest retained-evidence/custody records, active/provisional generations, rollback slots, prepared migrations, binding retention policy/tombstones) and becomes eligible only when those roots are empty. The repair-state root remains joined to DR-110/G08 and is not a self-update design here. This member does not design purge, does not invent a loss code, does not assign G19 state class, and does not score G12 doctor/purge honesty. Fixtures are unauthored.
retainedEvidence.passProperty: A referenced generation is not deleted. Removal deactivates; it does not emit a typed PURGED sealed-Run result. An invented purge, loss, or D9 code fails this specification. G12 and G19 are not scored. Pass all four D-002 platforms. Waiver of a referenced deletion is forbidden.
retainedEvidence.suppliedBy: crash-injection corpus class, conflicting-project-locks corpus class, and process-death corpus class. Not authored.
